notes.meaning: God gives Ezekiel a new message and commands him to wail over the terrible disaster coming upon Egypt. The call to weep and shout 'Alas for that day!' shows how sudden and shocking the downfall will be. Even before the invaders arrive, the prophet must announce that Egypt's destruction is certain.

The Day of the Lord is a time when God steps into human history to judge sin and bring down proud rulers. Here, it is pictured as a dark and cloudy day of trouble for Egypt and other foreign nations. It serves as a reminder that worldly empires cannot escape God's justice forever.

An invading army will strike Egypt with warfare, causing deep panic in neighbouring Cush, also known as Ethiopia. Egypt will lose its great wealth, and the institutions and leaders holding the nation together will be torn down. When a powerful nation falls, all the partners who relied on it shake with fear.

Egypt relied on foreign allies and hired soldiers from North Africa and surrounding regions to defend its borders. God warns that these mercenary troops and treaty partners will fall by the sword right alongside Egypt. Human alliances and paid armies cannot protect a nation when God brings it to account.

All the supporters and governors who hold up Egypt's power will collapse, ending the nation's boastful pride. The slaughter will sweep across the entire country, from Migdol in the far north to Syene in the far south. No corner of the land will escape the coming judgment.

Egypt will be left completely desolate, sharing the ruined state of other lands that have already been crushed by war. Her famous, crowded cities will sit in ruins like empty ghost towns. Even the richest civilization cannot guarantee its own survival.

God compares the coming war to a fire that sweeps through Egypt and shatters all her allies. When the flames consume their defenses, the people will finally realize that the Lord of Israel is the one true God. The fires of judgment expose the uselessness of every earthly protector.

Messengers will travel by ship up the Nile River to bring the terrifying news of Egypt's collapse to Cush. The people of Cush felt safe because they lived far away, but the report will shatter their easy confidence. God makes sure that news of His righteous acts reaches even those who feel untouched by danger.

God openly names King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon as the human instrument He will use to crush Egypt's huge population. Although Babylon acted out of its own imperial greed, the Lord was the one directing the outcome. Earthly kings remain tools in the hands of the sovereign God.

Nebuchadnezzar and his Babylonian army are described as the most ruthless and fierce among the nations. God permits these cruel invaders to draw their swords and fill Egypt with the bodies of the slain. A nation that once terrified others will now face a conqueror it cannot stop.

Drying up the canals and branches of the Nile means taking away Egypt's water supply, which provided both food and military defense. Handing the land over to wicked foreigners means God will strip away Egypt's wealth and leave it in the hands of brutal conquerors. Because the Lord has spoken it, this ruin is guaranteed to happen.

God promises to destroy the idols and carved images in Memphis, one of Egypt's greatest centers of pagan worship. He also declares that native Egyptian princes will no longer rule the land, leaving the nation paralyzed with fear. False gods and proud rulers always prove useless when God's judgment falls.

Judgment will fall upon every major region, from Pathros in the south to Zoan and Thebes. Zoan, an ancient city near where Israel once suffered as slaves, will be burned with fire, while the grand southern capital of Thebes will be shattered. God shows that no part of the empire is beyond His reach.

Pelusium was a key border fortress on Egypt's northeastern frontier, known as the stronghold that protected the kingdom from invaders. God promises to pour out His anger on this fortress and wipe out the massive crowds of Thebes. Even the strongest military gates cannot keep out the judgment of the Lord.

Pelusium will writhe in agony like a woman in labor as enemy troops break through its defenses, and Thebes will see its walls torn open. Memphis will face open attacks and distress in broad daylight. The horrors of war will leave Egypt's greatest cities in complete ruin.

The young warriors of On, a center of sun worship, and Pi-beseth will fall in battle. The remaining people of these famous religious cities will be marched off as prisoners into exile. Idolatrous shrines and the young soldiers who defend them will perish side by side.

Darkness will cover the frontier palace city of Tahpanhes as God breaks Egypt's power to rule over and oppress other peoples. A dark cloud of grief will hang over the city, and its daughters will be dragged off into captivity. When an empire uses its strength to burden others, God eventually breaks its heavy yoke.

By carrying out these severe punishments on Egypt, the Lord will prove His supreme power to everyone watching. Egypt had spent centuries trusting its own gods, but now the people will realize that Yahweh alone is the Lord. God makes Himself known when He humbles proud nations.

Ezekiel dates this prophecy to the spring of 586 BC, about three months before the Babylonians broke through Jerusalem's walls. At that time, Pharaoh's army had made a brief move to help Jerusalem, giving the Jews temporary hope. God speaks directly into that crisis to show that Egypt is entirely unable to rescue them.

God pictures Pharaoh's military power as a broken arm that has received no splint or bandage to heal. Because it was shattered by previous defeats, Egypt cannot regain enough strength to lift a sword in battle. Putting our trust in human strength only leads to disappointment when trouble comes.

God announces that He is set against Pharaoh and will break both of his arms—both the one already damaged and the one that still seemed strong. With both arms broken, the sword of military power will drop completely from the king's hands. No leader can defend himself once the Lord decides to take away his power.

The Lord declares that the people of Egypt will be taken captive and scattered across many foreign lands. This forced dispersion was the usual outcome for countries conquered by ancient world powers. God controls the history and homes of all nations according to His will.

The Lord will strengthen the arms of Babylon's king and place His own sword of judgment directly into Nebuchadnezzar's hands. At the same time, Pharaoh's broken arms will leave him groaning helplessly before his enemy like a dying soldier. Earthly rulers rise or fall purely because of God's sovereign choice.

Babylon will grow stronger while Pharaoh's arms fall completely limp and useless. When Nebuchadnezzar swings God's sword across the land of Egypt, everyone will see that the Lord alone directs the outcome. God's purpose in every national shift is to show that He is the true ruler of the world.

God repeats His promise that the Egyptians will be scattered among foreign nations so they will finally know that He is the Lord. Repeating this warning highlights that God's word is fixed and will surely take place. People come to recognize God's greatness when their own pride has been completely laid low.
